[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/29 (Mon) 03:29  
[FACT] User is interested in blockchain technology and its mechanisms.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Miners run full nodes to verify and add new transactions to the blockchain, validating every transaction in a block and checking adherence to consensus rules.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Bob the merchant uses a lite node that implements Simplified Payment Verification (SPV) to verify transactions quickly and efficiently.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A double-spend attack can occur if a malicious ISP controls a user's connections, allowing them to broadcast conflicting transactions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To successfully execute a double-spend attack, an attacker would need to control a significant portion of the network's mining power.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Bob checks the number of confirmations a transaction has received to determine its validity and likelihood of being reversed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Blocks can occasionally get orphaned if two miners discover blocks nearly simultaneously, leading to competing branches in the blockchain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The consensus branch is determined by the longest chain, which represents the most accumulated work in the proof-of-work consensus algorithm.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The rate of orphan blocks is affected by factors such as network propagation time, size of the mining network, and frequency of block discovery.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A formula for the rate of orphan blocks can be expressed as: Rate of Orphan Blocks = (Probability of Two Miners Discovering Blocks Nearly Simultaneously) x (Percentage of Mining Power Contributed by the Miner Who Discovers the Orphan Block).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability of two miners discovering blocks nearly simultaneously can be calculated as: Probability = (Propagation Time / Block Time) x (Percentage of Mining Power Contributed by the Miner Who Discovers the Orphan Block).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The percentage of mining power contributed by the miner who discovers the orphan block influences the rate of orphan blocks.
